title: 'It was the chance of our lives': After short exile in Ceuta, tens of thousands of young people return to Morocco
subhead: Spurred by messages on social media, around 50,000 people illegally crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta since Thursday, July 30, in an unprecedented influx. But most have already been forced to make the journey back.

subhead: Despite alarming statistics about the decline in time spent reading, literary gatherings in France are making a comeback, especially among women under 30.

title: Wildfire in southwest France: Local officials recount 10 days of battling the blaze
subhead: The prefect of the affected Gironde region, Sophie Brocas, and the head of its fire and rescue service, Marc Vermeulen, reflect on their management of the massive wildfire that has been raging since July 22 in an interview with Le Monde.

title: The new era of AI-powered search, which could 'change the web economy'
subhead: Since Wednesday, Google has started displaying artificial intelligence-generated responses, known as AI Overviews, for certain queries, rather than the traditional list of links. Website publishers and brands now fear for their visibility and are trying to find ways to respond.

title: French-American jazz duo DOMi & JD Beck release genre-defying second album
subhead: Endorsed by Herbie Hancock, DOMi & JD Beck's second album, 'Who Asked?' is hard to label, combining jazz, electro and indie pop, and experimenting with acoustic wind instruments like the clarinet, trombone and flute.

title: Kush, a synthetic and highly addictive drug, devastates Sierra Leone and Liberia
subhead: 'Africa under the influence' (2/6). Sold at a low price, kush causes rapid addiction and severe, often fatal, injuries. Photographer Gaël Turine traveled to Freetown and Monrovia to document the destruction wrought by this new synthetic drug among young people in Sierra Leone and Liberia.

title: France ramps up judicial action to prevent forest fires
subhead: Since July 23, 12 people have been referred to court for 'endangering the lives of others,' according to figures from the Bordeaux prosecutor's office, which announced tougher criminal action against the use of fire in forested areas.
